1115431_5611c395.text: Of 20 immunogold-labeled gap junctions, seven were large (328–1140 connexons), three of which were consistent with electrical synapses between interneurons; but nine were at axon terminal synapses, three of which were immediately adjacent to distinctive glutamate receptor-containing postsynaptic densities, forming mixed glutamatergic synapses

1115431_a3510045.text: Gap junctions also were on spines in stratum lucidum, stratum oriens, dentate gyrus, and hilus, on both interneurons and unidentified neurons

1115431_623fc68d.text: Twelve neuronal gap junctions were at glutamatergic mixed synapses [defined by the presence of PSDs (three), presence in spines (seven), or presence in identified axon terminals (two)]

1115431_08a02feb.text: In stratum oriens, one gap junction labeled for Cx36 was found on the shaft of a spiny dendrite, immediately adjacent to an immunogold-labeled glutamate receptor PSD, defining this as a glutamatergic mixed synapse, possibly involving a spiny interneuron or a CA3pyr dendrite within the infra-pyramidal bundle

1115431_6328c07d.text: widespread distribution of neuronal gap junctions in hippocampus, with most either at glutamatergic mixed synapses or in association with extrasynaptic glutamate receptor clusters.

1115431_a1a559eb.text: Additionally, glutamatergic neurons can form mixed synapses that combine chemical glutamatergic transmission with electrical coupling through gap junctions, as observed in CA3 pyramidal neurons (Hamzei-Sichani et al., 2012).
